external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser that communicates with the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application that receives browser traffic and places jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background worker that picks up queue jobs and performs the heavy work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue onto which the web application puts jobs and from which the background worker picks them up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: A database read and written by the background worker and used to keep application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The description does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the web application's settings and queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the worker's settings and database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks to application
data_flows.description: The user's browser communicates with the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: The web application places jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: picks up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker retrieves jobs from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up

data_flows.name: reads and writes database
data_flows.description: The background worker reads from and writes to the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.
data_flows.data_description: database records and application log records

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from the web application config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from the worker config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: outside our network
trust_boundaries.description: The area outside the system's network where the user's browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier behind the web tier containing the queue, worker and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config contains confidential data because it holds queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config contains confidential data because it holds database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds the worker's database credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The outside-our-network zone is tenant-controlled because it contains a user's browser outside the system's network.
assumptions.basis: The source places a user's browser outside our network, indicating a zone outside the system owner's control.

assumptions.assumption: The web tier is a network boundary because it is a distinct tier from the backend tier.
assumptions.basis: The source places the web application in the web tier and describes the backend tier as behind it.

assumptions.assumption: The backend tier is a network boundary because it is a distinct tier behind the web tier.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the queue, worker and database are in the backend tier, behind the web tier.
